candidates.brief: Explain why Starship cannot simply turn around after launch: its orbital path must line up with Starbase, so it circles Earth for about 21 hours before a deorbit burn and tower-catch attempt. Show how orbital mechanics, heat-shield reentry, guidance flaps and the final engine flip work—and why this matters for fully reusable rockets rather than just spectacle.
candidates.evidence_summary: SpaceX’s Flight 15 plan describes a roughly 21-hour coast after payload deployment before Starship’s orbit aligns with Starbase, followed by a controlled deorbit and conditional catch attempt. The mission is planned, not a guaranteed success. ([space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-will-launch-epic-double-catch-starship-flight-15-test-mission-on-nov-13?utm_source=openai))
candidates.science_angle: Orbital ground tracks, deorbit burns, atmospheric reentry, hypersonic heating and autonomous landing guidance.

candidates.brief: Use the viral freeway video to explain what a driverless car has to recognize during a traffic break: police vehicles, lane closures, unusual vehicle motion and conflicting road cues. Then explain the limits of autonomous driving systems, how remote assistance can provide context without remotely driving the car, and why emergency-response behavior is harder than ordinary lane following.
candidates.evidence_summary: A video reported on November 11, 2026 showed a driverless Waymo attempting to move around CHP vehicles during an apparent traffic break. Waymo says its vehicles can request human contextual assistance while retaining control of the vehicle. candidates.title: USB Colors Really Matter!
candidates.query: USB port colors blue black red meaning speed charging explained USB-IF
candidates.brief: Turn the viral USB-color question into a practical guide: blue commonly signals SuperSpeed USB, while black often indicates USB 2.0, but color is only a clue and not a guarantee. Explain bandwidth, charging, USB-C labeling and why viewers should check the printed specification before assuming a port’s speed.
candidates.evidence_summary: USB-IF recommends blue for USB 3.0 Standard-A receptacles and requires users to be able to distinguish USB 3.0 from USB 2.0, but leaves the exact visual method to manufacturers. That means port color is useful shorthand, not a universal rule. ([compliance.usb.org](https://compliance.usb.org/index.asp?Format=Standard&UpdateFile=USB3&utm_source=openai))
candidates.science_angle: High-speed differential signaling, bandwidth limits, connector standards, power delivery and labeling ambiguity.
